## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitone II

- **C5** (C) Windows: the DN2 tooling needs an m68k objdump; use WSL. `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}
- **C7** (C) Porting to a new OS version = re-locating, not re-applying. Diff decoded content, check bootstrap and updater separately, re-find every patch by masked pattern (`find`/`expect`) and pin the build by hash; inspect unfamiliar sections first. (Digitone II 1.11 vs 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes.) `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions} {dn2-cfw-release-history}
- **C8** (C) Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines).
- **C9** (C) After every install, open a project saved before it, and install the next build over the normal route. Old data meets new code only on the unit: a DN2 project with a stored row count out of range crashed stock and modded builds, Octatrack projects stalled when an effect layout changed, dn2mk2's MD/MM tracks went silent after an install, armio's USB audio repeated after a project change, and Overtone 1.0 broke the next USB update. A release test opens an old project and a stock project, changes project once, and installs the following build with Transfer. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I13](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change), [I21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install), [I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). [I73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i73-an-old-project-stopped-all-sound-on-a-sample-machine-mod) (an old project silenced every track), [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (mod data lost at a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT). `[hw]`
- **C12** (C) Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes}
- **D6** (D) Custom machine IDs are permanent once kits store them. Range 4-127. Claim `machine:<id>`. Known claims (Digitakt mk1, core 2.1): 4 = NEIGHBOR, 5 = DIGISLICER. Pick a free ID, then register it in [`devices/digitakt.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} D6b. Digitone II machine IDs: synths 5-31 and filters 6-31 are separate namespaces, permanent, and there is no allocator - agree IDs with other authors before shipping; saved sounds of an absent mod keep their ID and show as MISSING. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2} D6c. Analog Rytm MKII mod machines take the hidden slots 34-43 (from elekloader core-ar2 0.13 also the TEST slots 44-52), claimed as `machine:<slot>`. Kits store the slot; on a build without the mod the kit loads it as DISABLE. elekloader refuses two mods with the same slot, and Modwerk also records claims on its agent board. Each slot has fixed knob positions, so give meaning to a sound index, not to a knob letter. `[doc]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}
- **E2** (E) Persist a mod's own sound parameters through the stock edit event, not a writer of your own. On the Digitone II (1.11) an edit is written into the stored sound record at once, so unsaved edits survive a power cycle; the writer is `Sound::updateMirror` (`0x4004ca80`). dnfw's LFO4 values did not survive until its setter sent the stock whole-sound event (`SoundConfigChangedInfo`) through the sound's holder; `updateMirror` then re-serialised the sound with LFO4's lane. Confirmed on the unit: unsaved LFO4 edits survive a power cycle, and SAVE PROJECT stores them. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4}
- **E3** (E) Keep every stored count and select value in range, and stamp old projects after a layout change. Stock trusts what it loads: the DN2's song LOAD copies a stored row count without a check (21,503 rows instead of at most 99 crashed stock and modded builds alike), and an Octatrack select value outside its count stalled the sequencer on first play after an effect's layout changed. Clamp every count and enum a mod writes; when a build changes a stored layout, rewrite old projects' values on load. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count), [I28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject}
- **E5** (E) Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incidents: [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (Digitakt mk1: a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT drops kit spare bytes that LOAD PROJECT keeps), [I52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot).
- **F5** (F) Never run parsers across device generations (Digitone mk1 device ID 0x0D vs Digitone II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2). `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}
- **G9** (G) DSP rules the emulators cannot check (Digitone II, each reportedly silenced or crashed a real unit): whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock instruction encodings only (incl. sign bits of negative shift immediates), PRM loop/DAG/branch rules, no L2 above `0x200B0000`, never read unwritten DDR (power-on NaN), preserve registers at hooks (clobbered R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio), count memory accesses not instructions. Details and addresses in [`devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md). `[hw]` {dn2-skill-sharc} Incidents: [I8](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan), [I25](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i25-clobbering-r8-at-the-fx-bus-mixer-hook-lost-all-audio), [I26](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i26-a-boot-block-of-8n4-bytes-left-the-unit-silent), [I27](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip).

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [hw] Reported 2026-09-11: Transfer showed 100 % sent while the device bar froze near 80 %; stock 1.10E stalled over the same route, so the link was at fault, not the image. Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#719a2a9e`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L18))
- [hw] Fixes: prove the link with the stock firmware first; use a dedicated class-compliant USB-MIDI cable for long recovery transfers; disable Windows USB selective suspend and device power management; retry. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} (`flash-procedure#33d3b934`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L19))
- [hw] Proven on hardware: stock 1.10E via recovery (2026-09-08), stock 1.11 via recovery over a fixed link (2026-09-11); modified images via the normal update path. dnfw records no modified image completing the recovery route - recovery has been proven with stock only. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#eeccb444`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L20))
- [hw] A mod can break the normal USB update path without anyone noticing until the next update. On Overtone 1.0 (Digitone II), an OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing. The only way off it was the STARTUP menu over DIN, about 15 minutes. Test "install the next build over USB" as part of every release (rule A36). `[hw]` {overtone} ([I22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path)) (`recovery#aa79ffc2`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L19))
- [doc] MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#f6ed5a32`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:14](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L14))
- [doc] Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety} (`flash-procedure#243fba81`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L15))
- [doc] Back up with the `.dnx` backup before flashing; run `dnfw inspect` on the exact file you will send (build and patch only refuse output that does not verify). (`flash-procedure#386baed4`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L38))
- [doc] Keep the unmodified `.syx` in a firmware folder and never overwrite it with build output. (`flash-procedure#c54e3b5a`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L39))
- [doc] Change one thing per flash. (`flash-procedure#0debb1db`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L40))
- [doc] Do not patch the key material. (`flash-procedure#03c1c7d5`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:41](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L41))
- [doc] Do not start a flash on a crashing host (a previous workstation's `0x9F` crashes were tied to an NVIDIA driver). (`flash-procedure#0a1b43bb`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L42))
- [doc] The log records what was sent, not what is resident: write a row when stock goes back on. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} (`flash-procedure#55e888f0`, [hardware/common/flash-procedure.md:43](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/flash-procedure.md#L43))

- [doc] "Some upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap" right after the first restart; do not turn the power off then. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#065677fb`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L29))
- [doc] Downgrading is not supported and is at the user's own risk; user content may be lost. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#258d6d79`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L30))
- [doc] Digitakt II, first reboot after upgrading to OS 1.15: a file-system integrity check (up to a minute). - [doc] Heat +FX: in-OS path is SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with the file sent through MIDI In or USB MIDI In; the startup path takes MIDI In only. `[doc]` {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#2a7bab5e`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L32))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB1** eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry (TRIM is idempotent); fixed in dn2mk2 v0.40.
- **SB2** Song LOAD trusts a stored row count and halts the unit (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by the `songguard` mod (dn2_firmware_explore, also in dn2mk2): a damaged song loads empty; confirmed on hardware. Users: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`).
- **SB3** The USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: keep the container under 2 MiB; check the size in the build.
- **SB4** Auto-commit upload loses its "upload complete" event (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock). Workaround: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself.
- **SB5** LFO TRIG MODE ONE and HALF do not run one (half) cycle and hold (Digitone II, OS 1.11; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by the `lfolength` mod (dn2_firmware_explore; supersedes `lfohold`); confirmed on hardware on an audio track (2026-10-09), MIDI tracks in the emulator.

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I1** Stock eMMC TRIM fails with TRIM ERROR on a busy card. Cause: after CMD38 the stock busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt before it tests DAT0; a short TRIM that finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post, so the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout. Fix: read `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read, call only when idle; retry five times; ERASE PAUSED and resume on request (v0.40). Rules: A47.
- **I2** Stock song LOAD trusts a stored row count. Cause: song LOAD `0x400dea6a` copies `count` stored rows without checking it; the project held 21,503 rows instead of at most 99. Fix: repair the project (row count at record `+0x147`, storage version 4); mods must keep every count in range. Rules: E3.
- **I3** USB upgrade receiver does not check the 2 MiB limit. Cause: the receive buffer is 2 MiB and the receiver does not check the size. Fix: keep the container under `0x200000` bytes. Rules: A30,A9.
- **I4** Auto-commit upload loses its "complete" event on the first upload after boot. Cause: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" while the upgrade view is not open yet; the event is lost. Fix: upload without auto-commit, then send End(1), which checks the bytes and posts the event itself. Rules: A21.
- **I8** Power-on DDR holds garbage (often a NaN). Cause: DSP DDR is not cleared at power-on; the emulator zero-fills it and hides this. Fix: never read memory you did not write; fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests. Rules: G8,G9.
- **I9** A second application on the port corrupts SysEx replies. Cause: two clients share the USB MIDI port. Fix: close Transfer, Overbridge and DNX before a client run; check reply lengths. Rules: F7.
- **I70** A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller. Cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause. Fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes. Rules: A39.
- **I10** Byte-wise reads of uncached DMA buffers stalled the sequencer. Cause: the main OS sets CACR `0xa50ce100` / ACR0 `0x4007e020` (`0x40000000-0x47ffffff` cached); the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100` are uncached, and UM01 packed their slots with byte-wise reads. A first look at the bootstrap's CACR (cache off) gave a wrong conclusion. Fix: read each of the 14 SSI slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02): no lag with busy sequences. Rules: A48.
- **I12** A sample-machine mod could not create the storage it needed. Cause: R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one; stock FORMAT +DRIVE and the resets do not create it. Fix: R013 adds SYSTEM > FORMAT SAMPLES; formatting, Transfer capacity (~20 GB) and uploads passed on the unit. Rules: A49.
- **I13** USB audio repeated old audio after a project change. Cause: the TX selector follows RX completion and is no ownership grant; the build bound its queue head to a destination from an older phase. Fix: R011 picks the candidate from the current DMA START. Rules: C9.
- **I19** Patching a "free" zero run crashed the unit. Cause: the run was an array that the code fills at run time. Fix: two static checks (equal-stride gaps, referenced operands); only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both. Rules: D11,A43.
- **I21** MD and Monomachine tracks went silent after an install. Cause: unknown (suspected stale voice-slot state or state from an older version's project). Fix: none yet; test an old project after every install. Rules: C9.
- **I22** A mod broke the normal USB update path. Cause: the mod's build; fixed in 1.0.1. Fix: the STARTUP menu over DIN (~15 min); a release test that installs the next build over USB. Rules: A36,C9.
- **I25** Clobbering R8 at the FX-bus mixer hook lost all audio. Cause: the mixer takes R4 and R8 as arguments; the hook changed R8. Fix: preserve every register and flag that code after a hook reads; compare callee registers between stock and the build. Rules: G9.
- **I26** A boot block of 8n+4 bytes left the unit silent. Cause: the L2 instruction-cache line fill over the block's end faults on ECC. Fix: whole 32-byte boot blocks (`dspblocks.pad_lines`, `bootblocks.py`). Rules: G9.
- **I27** An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip. Cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR). Fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly. Rules: A41,G9.
- **I51** The sample popup did not open after switching Machines. Cause: the separate sampler SYN view was not selected when the Machine changed within the audio-track class. Generic notifications redrew the old stock view. Earlier tests manually reselected SYN and hid the missing lifecycle transition. No live capture established that every intermittent popup report shares this cause. Fix: R021 defers reconciliation to the existing UI poll, uses native selection and ownership, and avoids modal/selected-trig transitions; included in R022. Rules: C8.
- **I52** New project samples were missing after reboot. Cause: load notification ran the native incremental settings serializer, but the port updated its sample companion only during whole-project serialization. Both prepared working backup and fresh emulated boot retained an empty identity for the loaded slot. The frozen device's actual backup state was not captured. Fix: R022 refreshes the working sample companion in that settings worker under the existing project lock, validates owner/UID, and preserves explicit saved checkpoints. Rules: E5.
- **I65** A machine kind past the end of a label table froze Digitone II units. Cause: the label lookup picked the Monomachine label table by range; BOUNCE (kind 13) read past its end and walked address `0xEE` as a list. The emulator reads low memory as zeros, which hid it (I66 has the gate side). Fix: one explicit test per machine kind, a `machines` gate step, and a trap on any non-stock read below `0x40000000` in every emulator step (v0.45). Recovery used: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 2 (EMPTY RESET; the +Drive is kept), then flash v0.45. Rules: A53.
- **I68** Spring-reverb builds lost their sound on a Digitone II; no cause found offline. Cause: not found. An offline search ruled out illegal instructions and accesses, parity, FP exceptions, the stack, Elektron's code, timing in digikit's coupled emulator, and digikit's SHARC+ silicon rules (checked on every build, no hit). The one lead: the spring's output is exactly 0 from 1.4 s into FX kill and 78 s after a stop, as at both unit stops [inferred]. Fix: the spring is shelved; its six builds stay withdrawn. The author stopped blind device tests. The next test build (EEEM, a light morphing reverb in the reverb slot) sends the stock DSP's idle parks to a fault tone whose pitch names the fault (1500 Hz illegal instruction, 3000 Hz parity, 6000 Hz emulation or default handler, 1500 + 6000 Hz abort or stack check; a ~750 Hz buzz or silence is a hang). Rules: A16.
- **I71** A DSP load guard dropped a sample voice block after block. Cause: the frame-time guard left the sample voice out when a block ran short of time, and because a sample voice is retried in every block it came and went block by block instead of stopping. Fix: planned for v0.49: render the sample voices first, so time runs out on the heavy synth voices, and keep a dropped sample voice stopped until its next note, as PERC voices already are. Rules: A44.
- **I73** An old project stopped all sound on a sample-machine mod. Cause: unknown. The author's sampler model plays STRETCH, REPITCH and ONESHOT cleanly with odd stored STRT/LEN words (old 127, 120.00, out of range), so the stored data of the old project is the main suspect; not reproduced. Fix: none yet. The author plans two gate steps: projects saved on earlier builds played in the coupled emulator, and every stored control word driven through the DSP code. Rules: C9.
- **I74** Filter builds overloaded the DSP and broke USB audio. Cause: the right-hand effects chain was duplicated and ran for every voice. With it gated to sampler voices (R025), the model predicts about 81.7 % of the audio block with 16 voices; it leaves out interrupts, cache, DMA and USB. Fix: R025 runs the right effects chain only for sampler voices; R027 keeps that. Rules: A16,A37.
- **I37** A SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply. Cause: the emulator shifted every fractional multiply left; the PRM shifts only signed x signed. Fix: fixed in the emulator; `sharc_checks.py` calls stock routines and compares. Rules: C10.
- **I39** The default compression level corrupted a DN2 image. Cause: section 4's in-place loader has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's `-l 3` gives -39,318. Stock DT2 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). Fix: check the margin at every loader stage; a dense packer. Rules: A14.
- **I42** Checks reported success about work they never did. Cause: snapshot harnesses cleared code no real boot ran; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after its coverage section was deleted; an emulator call returned 0 for a present value. Fix: every check gets a control that must fail. Rules: C8.
- **I66** A feature that crosses ColdFire and DSP passed the gate and failed on units. Cause: unknown. The gate never ran the ColdFire and the DSP together. Per the v0.48 notes the recorder trigs fired and takes were made, but the track never played its buffer. Fix: BOUNCE removed from the menu in v0.47 and its code removed in v0.48 (old projects load, the track silent). v0.48 adds a coupled emulator that runs both processors one audio block at a time (faithful in order and content, not in timing margins) and the first gate step on it; FLEX, the replacement, is to be tested from recording to playback on it. Rules: C4,C2.
- **I43** Recovery stalled at ~80 %: the MIDI link, not the image. Cause: a USB MIDI interface went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets. Fix: a MIDI interface that stays awake for the ~12-15 min transfer. Rules: A11,A20.
- **I47** Stock storage resets did not create the sample filesystem. Cause: stock has no such filesystem on the DN2. Fix: the mod's own FORMAT SAMPLES (R013). Rules: A3,A49.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O20** DT2/DN2 stock intro frame rate: A) 30 Hz: digikit's PIT3 model (PCSR `0x093f`, PMR 8593), so the first scene table's 175 frames last 5.8 s (finding 117) B) 15 Hz: digikit's earlier emulator notes derive it from divisor 1024 (66.67 ms per frame; finding 07)
- **O19** DN2 SHARC L2 between `0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000`: A) in use: stock data words point to `0x200918c0`, `0x200c0008` and `0x200c1f84` (dnfw), so Digiwerk keeps new data out of the whole range and lists `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` as candidates B) usable: the DN2 modding skill places boot blocks at `0x20090000` (code) and `0x20098000` (data), hardware-proven, and sets the ceiling at `0x200b0000`; elekloader's master-output mod (`0x20090000-0x20098000`) ran on a unit for ten minutes, and its machines take `0x20090000-0x200b0000`
- **O16** What section 8 is for: A) the Outbox 8 accessory (dnfw: the image arrived in the DN2 release that added Outbox support; an inference from timing) B) the panel MCU firmware (analog-emu)
- **O6** DN2 1.11 parameter table base: A) `0x401f7fc8` (skill's map) B) `0x401f7fc4` (dnfw memory map)
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O9** Bootstrap write protection: A) DYB lock on sector `0x40000` (Spansion S25FL command) B) the DN2 board photographed carries a Winbond W25Q128JV, on which that lock does nothing
- **O12** DN2 load model: A) Digiwerk: load = (1.30 x instructions + 11k) / 666,667, predicted ~74 % B) the unit showed ~50-60 %
- **O13** Free top of the SHARC L1 blocks (DN2): A) static: L1 block 3 tail and block 1/2 tails are free (Digiwerk T3.2) B) the startup enables the caches there, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache
- **O15** DN2 stock DSP load at idle: A) ~63-65 % flat whatever plays (dnfw / Digiwerk idle-task method) B) ~80 % outside the idle task with nothing playing, falling to 65 % with 64 notes (elekloader dspbusy, 1,024-block windows)
- **O24** Digitakt II NRPN numbers (OS 1.17): A) the OS 1.17 manual: track mute 1:101, track level 1:100, pattern mute 1:104, master overdrive 2:37, filter env depth 1:23, filter base/width 1:51/1:52, portamento 3:7/3:8 B) midi.guide's data: 1:108, 1:110, 1:109, 2:50, 1:26, 1:24/1:25, 3:6/3:7 (the mute and level numbers match the Digitone II's)

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H18** (stock) The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod. Test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.
- **H19** (stock) The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20). Test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).
- **H23** (stock) The ~4 KB cut in long MidiRpc LIST replies is in the stock reply router, not in a mod: an unpaged listing of a 256-entry table store on a modded DN2 came back as 3,997 bytes, correct up to entry 125 and garbage after; pages of 64 were clean. Test: On stock, list a +Drive folder with more than 130 entries in one unpaged request (DNX or Elektroid) and compare the reply length and the tail with a paged listing. Until settled, page listings at 64 entries or fewer.
- **H24** (stock) The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too. Test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.
- **H8** (probe) The DN2's digikit flash cave `0x402fb7a8` (2,136 B on 1.11) keeps its bytes through a cold boot, as the DT2's `0x403117c4` does. Test: A canary in the cave, read back after a cold boot and after playback. Combine with H9.
- **H10** (probe) DN2 L2 `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is not written by stock in normal use (O19). Test: A canary or a write watch over the range during playback, pattern changes and a save (T24).
- **H11** (probe) DN2 RAM `0x46700000-0x46701300` is written by stock only when a +Drive transfer is over 60,672 bytes (S17: project save and load reach it). Test: A canary at `0x46700000`, read back after loading a large sample or project from +Drive.
- **H12** (probe) Direct hook writes may race reply publication on a DN2. Digikit measured 3,995 of 4,000 zero diagnostic words on a DT2; its own diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's record in the DN2 emulator. Silicon DMA timing remains unmeasured. Test: Compare a hook's direct counter writes with static-word publication at block tail, without clearing prior reply records; count arrivals on the ColdFire side.
- **H13** (build) SIMD loads or stores into L2 byte space hang the DN2's DSP as they hang the DT2's (same core, same IMASK). Test: A one-variable probe image with one SIMD L2 access behind a key press; recovery by power cycle.
- **H15** (build) On the DN2, a single late DSP block is a one-block dropout that recovers, as on the DT2; the "silence until power cycle" reports came from sustained overload. Test: Provoke single late blocks (a burn loop on a key press) and count them on the DSP side; then hold an overload for seconds.
- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T8** (needs files, effort M) Build an address-translation table DN2 1.11 <-> 1.12 from shared anchors (tool: [`scripts/anchor_translate.py`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/scripts/anchor_translate.py), 2026-11-11: you supply both images; it reports per address whether the translation is exact, bracketed, one-sided or ambiguous)
- **T9** (needs unit, effort M) Measure DN2 load with both meters (dnfw idle-task and elekloader dspbusy) in the same states, then calibrate a cost model (dn2mk2's instructions + 4 x L2 + 10 x DDR is a start)
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)
- **T14** (needs unit + emulator, effort M) Fix or document digikit's EMAC fractional-mode emulation against a unit measurement
- **T16** (needs unit, effort S) Save a project on a grown parameter table, load it on stock, record what happens
- **T18** (needs files, effort M) Document the project file formats (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`) beyond song slots
- **T24** (needs emulator, then unit, effort S) Watch DN2 SHARC L2 `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` for stock writes during playback, pattern changes and a save (emulator write watch first, then a canary on a unit); settles O19

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

Measured median per block: DT2 666,582, DN2 666,784 (digikit); DN2 666,706 (elekloader's idle-task meter); the owner's idle counter on a DT2 agrees. {digikit-f103} {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {own-dt2-notes} — `dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck#e9d9674c` [hardware/common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md:8](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md#L8) · Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. - [doc] [hw] Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old} — `firmware-container#0682353e` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L34) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections

- [hw] The DN2's code region has no free run of even 24 bytes. Zero runs exist in the constants region, and code there does execute (a boot-path cave printed "CAVE RAN!!!" on a real DN2). One "free" run was an array the code fills at run time: patching it crashed the unit, and the emulator watch read zeros. Two static checks catch most cases: a fixed stride between equal gaps marks an array, and `lea`/`pea`/`move.l #` operands mark referenced space. - [hw] Step states: at decoded `4 + 1187*(track-1) + 2*(step-1)`, two bytes per step, 16 tracks x 128 steps. Odd-step trig `03 81`, even-step trig `03 91`. `03 90` / `03 80` (bit 0 clear) is not an occupied step. First byte `0x78` = trigless trig (parameter automation, no note). — `sysex-and-midi#a9ded8ee` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L62) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
- [hw] Trigger records: at decoded `18996`, 6 bytes each, up to 8,192 records. Fields: track, step, note, velocity (`0xFF` = track default), length index (`0xFF` = inherit), and a signed micro-timing byte (1/384 note, -23..+23). - [doc] [hw] Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio} — `sysex-and-midi#1d9d72a8` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:132](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L132) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)

- [hw] The frame is longer than its data (elekloader core-dn2 0.3). The driver sends a 0xabc-byte frame but writes data halfwords only for the first 0xa80 bytes; for the rest it writes only command halfwords. So the tail from byte 0xa80 keeps whatever you write there before the call, and stock leaves it zero and ignores it on the DSP side. The driver's transmit queue is at `0x80002510` (one 32-bit entry per frame halfword, command half first); the frame sender calls the driver at `0x40025e9e`. The DSP reads tail word k as halfword 2k+1 above halfword 2k. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} — `digitone-2-internals#a3028f51` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L53) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)

- [hw] The in-place loader is the hidden size limit. Section 4's loader (`0x8000357c`, stage `0x40200000`) has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's default compression level (`-l 3`) gives -39,318 and corrupts the image. Every build needs a margin >= 0 at both loader stages; elekloader's default packer produced a container too large for the receive buffer, so the DN2 build uses a dense packer (`codec/dense.py`). Stock Digitakt II 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} ([I39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image)) — `digitone-2-internals#b00c31b9` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:92](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L92) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)

- [hw] The SHARC's filter accelerators, read on a DN2 (accelprobe, 2026-10-17). The ADSP-21569 has IIR0 and FIR0; the DN2 1.11 engine uses neither. Only 22 of 76 result words matched the models built from the hardware reference; the chip differs in three ways: IIR0 feeds stored word 5 of a biquad into the output: y = A0 x + s1, then s1 = (A1 x + s2) + B1 y and s2 = A2 x + B2 y, each step rounded to float32 (all 40 outputs and 4 states match). FIR0 adds its four partial sums in pairs, (acc0 + acc1) + (acc2 + acc3). In ACM mode the chip writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to a TCB's INIDX and 0 to OUTIDX after a window, the other way round from the hardware reference. Speed bounds, including setup: at most about 22 cycles per biquad-sample and 4.5 per tap-sample. ADI's application note gives the theoretical rates as 6 cycles per biquad (one MAC unit) and about 0.25 cycles per tap and sample (four MAC units), and says the coefficient and state preload dominates small jobs, which fits these bounds from jobs of 8-16 samples {adi-ee408}. The INIDX/OUTIDX write-back in ACM is not described there. digikit's models were corrected to match all 76 words. Same silicon on the DT2 ([crosscheck](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). `[hw]` {dn2-accel} — `digitone-2-internals#fdd6c202` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L119) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
- [hw] ColdFire tasks on a unit (DN2 1.11, read with the USB probe): The context switch is at `0x40000410-0x40000458`; the ready table at `0x4664ac9c` holds one list head per priority; higher numbers run first. Prio 0 never runs; prio 1 is the real idle loop (entry `0x400cec98`, parked at `0x400cf0e2`); the MIDI task (prio 7) answers the probe. Stack high-water marks after a busy pattern and a save: the fullest is a 2,048-byte prio-10 stack at 27 %; the main application's 160 KiB stack peaked at 1.5 %. Interrupts run on the current task's stack. ColdFire CPU 58-61 % whatever plays, almost all of it the audio ISR; a pattern raises the ISR's worst frame (75-83 % in a busy one), and SAVE PROJECT takes 100 % for about a second. `[hw]` {dn2-cftasks} — `digitone-2-internals#7d4ead03` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:124](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L124) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)

- [hw] How to tell a stop from the sound `[hw]` (inferred from the handler, matching every failed build): Silence (or a buzz from replayed pages) means a trap. The core sits in a high-priority handler, so the audio service can no longer run. A stuck tone (the output DMA replaying its last two pages, ~750 Hz) means a task-level stall, such as an endless loop, while the audio interrupt still runs. In both cases the ColdFire and UI keep running. — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#224424a8` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L66) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
- [hw] ILOPI is what toolchains miss: an encoding that selas emits and every decoder accepts, but the chip rejects. Examples are negative shift immediates and selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` (Type 5a), which put the wrong source code for every register from PC up, so `R0 = EMUCLK` became `R0 = LCNTR`. Use the compressed forms. `[hw]` {dn2-stall} ([I27](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip)) — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#0432f880` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L70) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
- [hw] L1 block 2 is not free just because the image leaves it empty: the PM data cache lives in L1 block 2 (and the I-cache in block 3), sized at boot by `SHL1C_CFG`. Code ending exactly at the last written word lets the sequencer prefetch never-written L1, which can raise a parity trap. Keep written memory after your last instruction. `[hw]` {dn2-dspstop} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#256a82ad` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:71](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L71) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)

- [hw] LOOP-ISA: last 11 instructions of a hardware loop (all of a short loop) must be legacy 48-bit ISA - stock 1.11 obeys it in all 286 loops ([rule A45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md)). LOOP-END: nested loops must not share an end address. LOOP-LCE: no `IF NOT LCE` in the last 11 instructions of a counter loop. LOOP-CALL: no CALL in the last 5 instructions of a loop. BRANCH-12: at least 12 valid 48-bit instructions' worth of code after every branch. BRANCH-WIN: no two branches in one 48-bit (3 short-word) window. DAG-SAME: no same-DAG DAG-register store and no post-modify same-DAG DAG-register load ("the root cause of silent units"; stock real code has zero of either). PRM references 4-14, 4-41, 4-42, 4-44. The checker reports only violations not present in a stock baseline. `[hw]` — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#3361709d` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:57](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L57) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
- [hw] Upload pitfall `[hw]`: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" to the upgrade view as the last block is parsed; on the first upload after a boot that view is not open yet, the event is lost and the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving". The skill therefore sends Start without auto-commit, all blocks, waits a few seconds, then End(1) - the End handler checks every byte arrived and posts the event itself; the stock OS then validates the container and asks UPGRADE OS NOW? (press YES). Keep USB silent while it writes flash (~90 s), then ping until it answers; one upload, no retries. Raw OS SysEx sent over USB to the running OS is ignored. Python + mido can hang at exit in CoreMIDI. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} {dn2-skill-setup} ([I4](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i4-auto-commit-upload-loses-its-complete-event-on-the-first-upload-after-boot)) — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#6cb77719` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L62) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)

- [hw] C/asm is compiled with m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os` (no libc) and linked at `0x46800000` (free on 1.11) by `dnfw.patch.cbuild`; dnfw's 138-byte startup loader copies the appended `DNFW` area there at boot and calls your init; every hook site is checked against the stock bytes before it is overwritten - a wrong address fails the build; `context()` asserts bytes a hook relies on without writing them; section 3 is recompressed and the container re-signed. API shape: `jsr(addr, stub, stock=...)` (6 bytes), `jmp(addr, stub, displaced=N)` (the stub replays the displaced bytes), `patch(addr, old, new, why)`. `[hw]` Same toolchain as summarised in [`digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md). — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#6b11b4ee` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:66](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L66) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
- [hw] Flash space is the binding limit (2 MiB upgrade buffer): dnfw's packer is greedy with a one-step lazy look-ahead over a 32-deep match chain; a 192-deep chain packs MAIN OS 0.8 % and section 7 0.5 % smaller within the same format and window (depth 1024 packs worse); pure-Python aPLib costs ~20-50 s per section in CPython, ~3 s in PyPy; a content-keyed cache skips unchanged sections. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#ccf8ab74` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:67](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L67) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)

The emulator zero-fills DDR and hides this: fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} ([I8](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan)) — `digitone-2-os111-reference#329753c6` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L33) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
- [hw] Timing: the DSP renders on the codec clock and does not wait for the ColdFire. A frame that arrives after render started is dropped and the previous frame repeats, including its note-on masks ("the trig lights, no sound"). This is what happens when the ColdFire audio ISR overruns. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#f754d310` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L51) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
- [hw] Audio ISR budget `[hw]`: period ~0.67 ms per block; stock already uses ~64 % during playback; code at `0x46xxxxxx` costs roughly 4x more cycles per instruction than stock (DDR + cache misses) while SRAM at `0x8000xxxx` is cheap. Keep ISR C short, non-blocking, allocation-free; defer per-note work; count DDR accesses, not instructions. A laggy UI usually means ISR work is too heavy. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#adcbfafe` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:58](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L58) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [hw] Cache map (OS 1.11 and 1.12): the bootstrap leaves the data cache off (CACR `0x000cc100`), but the main OS start-up at `0x40000554` writes CACR `0xa50ce100` and ACR0 `0x4007e020`: `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` is cached copyback, everything else uncached, including the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100`. Reading those buffers byte by byte from a mod is slow enough to stall the sequencer: Digiwerk's first multichannel USB build (UM01) packed the SSI slots with byte-wise uncached reads and lagged until unusable; reading each of the 14 slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02) ran on the unit with busy sequences and no lag. Checking only the bootstrap's CACR gave a wrong "cache off" conclusion first, corrected the same day. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-usb} ([I10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i10-byte-wise-reads-of-uncached-dma-buffers-stalled-the-sequencer)) — `digitone-2#5b5150bb` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L37) · Digitone II / Architecture
- [hw] Board PCBA0109B, read from photographs of the parts (dnfw `docs/hardware.md`, 2026-09-12) {dn2-hw}. The same board number as the Digitakt II is reported. CPU: ColdFire MCF5441SCMJ250 (MCF5441x, 250 MHz). Not the V4e that older notes inherited from the Octatrack. RAM: NANYA NT5TU128M8HE-AC, 128 MB DDR2. Flash: Winbond W25Q128JV (16 MB SPI NOR, by the ColdFire). Storage: Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 (32 GB eMMC). DSP: ADSP-21569 (KBCZ10) with its own Kingston DDR3 beside it. Codec: AKM AK4621EF, 20 MHz crystal by the SHARC. There is no flash chip by the DSP: the ColdFire boots the SHARC (section 7 is its boot stream). `[hw]` (photos) — `digitone-2#eaed5eac` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L40) · Digitone II / Architecture

- [hw] Stock eMMC TRIM can fail with TRIM ERROR on a busy card (OS 1.11). A unit running dn2mk2 v0.39 stopped with TRIM ERROR at two different sector ranges while erasing mod data. dn2mk2's reading of the stock code: TRIM `0x4012c4b2` fails only when CMD35/36/38 get no answer (command timeout); after CMD38 the busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt (`0x4012c53e`) before testing DAT0 (`0x4012c544`), so a short TRIM whose card finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post (`0x4461b6c0`), the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once, and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout. v0.40's fix: read the eSDHC present-state register `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read and call only when the card is idle; retry a failed call five times (TRIM is idempotent); report ERASE PAUSED and continue on request. The error is `[hw]`; the race is a static reading of stock code, not seen on the bus. Anything that issues TRIMs through the stock driver on a DN2 (and, not checked, a DT2 with the same driver) should do the same. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v040} ([I1](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i1-stock-emmc-trim-fails-with-trim-error-on-a-busy-card)) — `digitone-2#213cde96` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:99](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L99) · Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)

- [emu] Frame: 0xa80 bytes from `0x80005e60`, sent by DSPI2 (16-bit DMA, 1,374 halfwords); the reply arrives at `0x800053a4`, every block (1,500/s). All send-FX, compressor, external-input and master parameters are one block of big-endian words at `0x9fa + 2*(k-25)` (`k` = the parameter row's mirror index; chorus is k 25-31). Compressor routing is at `0xd4` (track bits) and `0xd6`. 16 per-voice rows of `0x92` bytes start at `0xda`. A row is a voice, not a track: a track parameter goes to every row whose owner (`0xa5a + 2r`) is that track. `[emu]` — `digitone-2-internals#035a1762` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L39) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)

- [emu] Coupled emulator (v0.48): dn2mk2 now runs the ColdFire image (digikit's emulator) and the SHARC image together, one audio block of 32 frames at a time: the audio interrupt once per block, the sequencer timer at its exact rate but up to one block late in phase, one ColdFire packet per block to the DSP and the DSP's status one block later. Its own audit calls this faithful in order and content, not in timing: an interrupt never lands mid-UI code, a DSP overrun is not modelled, and the default "fast" mode runs the UI's 60 Hz tick about 90x too often (the "faithful" mode gets 59 of 60 ticks a second). The unit's ColdFire spends about 56 % in the audio interrupt with the sequencer stopped. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-v048} (I66) — `digitone-2-internals#6a079064` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:151](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L151) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
- [emu] FLEX replaces BOUNCE (machine type 17, BOUNCE's, so older projects open their BOUNCE track as FLEX with no conversion code). Moving voice state from DDR to L2 `0x200A0000-0x200A8000` (a range other mods proved on units) was their largest expected saving. - [emu] Incremental working-state updates are a separate persistence path from whole-project saves. In armio's port, sample load/unload updates a separate identity companion and sends the native ProjectSettings notification. Its queued worker `0x400469E2` calls settings serializer `0x400DF57A` at `0x400469FE`; it does not pass through whole-project serializer `0x400E1494`. The extension had been attached only to the latter, so the native settings mirror advanced while the added sample mirror stayed stale. The alternating boot snapshots at sectors `0x40000` / `0x48000` are separate from explicitly saved project slots (see the existing [storage map](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md)). R020 replay reproduced a new identity absent from the prepared backup and from a fresh emulated boot. R022 updates the working companion at the narrow settings-worker callsite under the existing project mutex, checking destination, owner, readiness and matching UIDs; explicit saved companions remain untouched. Unchanged identities skip the 16 KiB copy/CRC. Load, unload, fresh-boot restore and failure guards passed native replay; physical shutdown and freeze recovery are unverified. These extension defects are not evidence of a stock DN2 autosave bug. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot)) — `digitone-2#ca8d216d` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L69) · Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)
- [emu] A Machine change can leave a port's old SYN view attached even when the Sound has changed. Native selection reselects the view when audio/MIDI classification changes; stock synth to a ported sampler remains an audio track. Generic Project, ActiveTrack and Sound notifications redraw but do not replace the view. R020 replay reproduced knob D reaching the stock handler after switching to all six samplers. R021, included in R022, reconciles the exposed SYN view through the existing factory and native selector on the next UI poll, deferring during modal ownership, selected-trig edits, construction and expired ownership. Ten transitions and nine guards passed. Earlier tests explicitly selected SYN before turning D and therefore repaired the state they were meant to test. Hardware confirmation is pending. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines)) — `digitone-2#21d53614` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L70) · Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)

- [doc] At H2/H3 SIMD is off and no DO loop is active. The stock FX state lives in DDR: chorus `0x80459388`, delay `0x8005912c` (rings of 524,288 floats, max 8 s), reverb `0x80000018`. Three are byte-identical; in the other three every differing byte is a PC-relative call offset (same target) or one table-pointer literal. All call the same reciprocal helper at sw `0x1c06ba` in both images (RECIPS plus Newton steps, the helper behind A35's divide cost). - [doc] The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. - [doc] Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola} — `firmware-container#099deb5e` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L33) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections

- [doc] Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#df3a4b13` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:89](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L89) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
- [doc] SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#aec8faff` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L90) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)

- [doc] No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm} — `memory-maps#40215568` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L22) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)

DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. - [doc] The range from `0x46700000` up to `0x46710000` is not free. On 1.12 it holds the end of the DMA buffers; on 1.11 the MMC bounce buffer reaches `0x46701300`. dnfw's lfo4 state sat at `0x46700000` until 2026-10-11 and corrupted every project saved on an LFO4 unit (the bounce buffer carries each piece of a project on save and load); it now lives in the first block of stock's heap (`0x4464abf0`). dnfw's remaining `0x4670xxxx` chunks (from `0x46708000`) are above the 1.11 DMA section (`0x466b8000-0x46701340`) but inside the 1.12 one, so they must move for a 1.12 port. The "25.3 MB unclaimed above BSS" figure in dnfw's memory map missed these alias references. The skill's "`0x46700000..0x46900000` unused, hardware-confirmed" disagrees: see [CONFLICTS S17](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md). `[doc]` — `memory-maps#7046340b` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:57](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L57) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)

- [doc] Digitone II library contains Digitone mk1 preset files, which use a second container format (refuse foreign formats by magic bytes). `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio} — `sysex-and-midi#e2827ea8` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L15) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
- [doc] The same 7-bit packing: groups of one header byte plus up to 7 data bytes; header bit 6 holds the MSB of the first data byte, bit 0 that of the seventh; a short last group keeps its header. syxgrid's DN2 field "control byte 101506, mask `0x40`, payload 101507" is exactly this rule (first byte of a group). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#4d1b4b03` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L32) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] The same checksum and count: checksum = sum of the packed payload bytes (header bytes included) mod 2^14, sent as two 7-bit bytes, high first; count = packed length + 5 (checksum, count and `F7`), also mod 2^14. syxgrid recomputed the checksum over raw bytes `[10, 114113)` and matched the DN2's own on every fixture. A DN2 pattern message is 114,118 bytes, so its count field wraps; tools must not use it as a length. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#2af849a2` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L33) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#7642b2b0` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L35) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Device byte in dumps: Rytm (libanalogrytm's era, MKI) `0x07`; Digitakt `0x0A`; Digitakt II `0x14`; Digitone II `0x15`. A DN2 answered only `0x15` in a sweep and ignored `0x0B-0x0E`, `0x14` and `0x16`. The same bytes appear in the OS files ([`firmware-container.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} Three different device ids.
