- [doc] Two projects compared selache's VISA decoder with digikit's table decoder on the DN2 stock program, and agree on where each is wrong. The test: walk instruction by instruction between known starts (branch targets, `cjump` sites, DO-loop ends) and see who lands exactly. `[doc]` {dn2-selache} {dn2-cfw-t31} selache's disassembler gives some 48-bit forms as 32-bit (Type 3a `59be`, Type 4a `6a3e`, Type 7a `043e`, Type 16a `9980`) and one 32-bit form as 48-bit (Type 3b `593e`); DO-loop ends land on the table decoder's starts 85 of 85 times, on selache's 64 of 85, and selache prints most DO offsets with bit 23 set. digikit's table had Type 2b wrong (the programming guide's `000000011`, not the reference's `110000000`; selache won 119 to 0) and wrongly ruled out `Type10a_rel` in VISA; both fixed in digikit#31. Its `undoc16/48` forms are still provisional. A two-byte-late start still lands 94.9 % of spans, because VISA resynchronises within a few instructions. A decoder's score means something only against that control. — `toolchain-and-emulators#31699a85` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:23](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L23) · Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
- [doc] Disassembled text is not a patch format. 11,440 distinct encodings from the DN2's L2 program, each disassembled with selmap and reassembled alone with selas: 83.9 % came back identical; 1,265 kept their width but lost register fields the text does not show (`bitrev`, `modify`, `dm` moves); 216 changed width; 320 printed forms could not be parsed; 40 crashed the assembler. A 48-bit `nop` reassembles as the 16-bit one. Patch from source, and compare bytes (rule A41). `[doc]` {dn2-selache} — `toolchain-and-emulators#e8d30f6c` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:27](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L27) · Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
- [doc] digikit (current home ElekLabs/digikit, `[doc]` {digikit}): native Rust emulator running ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together with front panel, display and audio; web panel (WASM) and Tauri desktop app; `patchkit` applies modules to the user's own `.syx` and refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8; headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes; control socket for patch injection; ColdFire/DSP analysis databases and Ghidra tooling. Targets: Digitakt II 1.17 (also runs 1.16; 1.15C for old analysis), Digitone II 1.12 (also runs 1.11; 1.10E for old analysis). Caveats: DSP not real-time yet; browser host parked on `wip/browser-host`; no patched firmware installed on a device by the author; bootstrap-menu recovery untested on hardware. AGPL-3.0-or-later with NOTICE terms asking for the credit "digikit by Em D". — `toolchain-and-emulators#936e3acb` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:50](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L50) · Toolchains and emulators / Emulators
- [doc] Earlier digikit README (m-dwyer/digikit, {digikit-old}) described a Python/Unicorn design: ColdFire emulator for Digitakt II / Digitone II; patched Unicorn m68k (SR read, CCR sync, EMAC MAC with load; stock Unicorn refused); ColdFire-aware disassembler because Capstone misses MVS/MVZ and FF1; first run needs a cold boot of a few minutes to build snapshots; about 10M instructions/s. Works: core, interrupt controllers, PIT, DMA timers, eDMA, front-panel TX, display, SD/MMC up to identification. Missing then: DSP (no audio), input path, block storage - partly superseded by the Rust version above. `[doc]` {digikit-old} — `toolchain-and-emulators#6a21af16` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L51) · Toolchains and emulators / Emulators
- [doc] Elektron Emu (xerydian): five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) running each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU - Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles; the user supplies the `.syx` in a per-machine folder; +Drive emulated and persisted, WAV loading on DT2/Rytm/DN2; Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler; otherwise a slow interpreter that renders offline only); limits: Rytm analog voices are a custom model that does not sound like the machine, Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; 2 commits, no licence stated. `[doc]` {elektron-emu} — `toolchain-and-emulators#d1f1bb43` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L81) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] Their safety lesson: stock code never puts a load into an I register directly before a 48-bit instruction that uses it (0 of ~14 cases; there is always work in between). The SHARC emulator does not model the pipeline, so the cautious pass refuses that pairing. Copy the rule: do not create instruction pairings the stock code never has. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#5405dad6` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:17](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L17) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
- [doc] Where DSP code may live, after the probe study (Digiwerk PB01 findings, static, 2026-10-23) {dn2-cfw-pb01}: L1 block 1 above `0x2e4f46` gives about 12 KB, not the 45 KB of the static map, because the build keeps the edge for a 32 KB DM cache. Block 3's tail is the 16 KB I-cache. `0x315f8c-0x318000` in block 2 depends on whether the PM cache there is 16 or 32 KB. Code placed there stopped the DSP on a unit (CMP2's LOW MUP stop), so builds refuse it. L2 candidates: `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` (38,532 B) and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` (229,376 B). `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is kept free of data by the build. Other projects use part of that range on units: [CONFLICTS O19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md). Section 7 can grow ~150 KB before its 1 MiB limit. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#2f8ffb44` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L18) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
- [doc] Measuring per-stage cycles on the unit (dnfw `waverider-loadmap.md`): Chosen jumps and calls go through a 12-byte stub that reads EMUCLK and adds the cycles since the previous mark to the running segment. A null segment measures the marks' own cost. Results publish through reply word 2, half a record per block. A reusable recipe for any DSP mod. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#b2a758b9` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L32) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
- [doc] Notes: MIDI tracks have no voice limit in the output engine; the "4 notes" are only the UI's NOT2-NOT4 rows. A pattern's note pool holds 8,192 notes, with at most 16 notes per step. The MIDI note-output length is a byte counter over a 1,024-byte buffer. Stock 1.12 plays more than 4 notes per trig from a modded project. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#34a45f01` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:47](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L47) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
- [doc] DSP free memory (static): L1 block 2 is never written by the stream (128 KB), the L1 block 1 tail `0x2dd52c-0x2effff`, and L2 from `0x2008823c`. Correction: the startup turns on all three L1 caches, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache, not free. dnfw's proven code area is `0x2dd600-0x2e7000`. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#9ccff0b2` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L52) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)

What is missing is exactly the audio engine: the per-slot dispatch `0x1c642a`, the per-track loop and unpack, and the sample players. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#a7aeacd0` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:60](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L60) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)

- [doc] The audio slots are configuration, not constants: the engine indexes the TDM frame through bytes at `0x80005366-0x80005368` (enable and slot pair), set by an applier (`0x40025982`) from settings and the kit. A per-stream routing mod would change those bytes. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#51592672` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L69) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The three ColdFire <-> SHARC layers (dnfw `audio-dma.md`, `dsp-control-block.md`, lalzart cross-check)
- [doc] Link alignment: a routine searches the receive half for the marker `0x007FFFFF` and, on a hit, slips the DMA by two frames by patching CITER/BITER. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-internals#ff0e5b1a` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:70](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L70) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The three ColdFire <-> SHARC layers (dnfw `audio-dma.md`, `dsp-control-block.md`, lalzart cross-check)
- [doc] MAIN OS = section id 3 of the ELE3 container; load address `0x40000400` on Digitone II and Digitone mk1; big-endian; 16-byte header, first instruction `46 FC 27 00` (`MOVE #$2700,SR`) at `0x40000410`. Depacked size: DN2 1.10E 3,085,696 B, DN2 1.11 about 3.19 MB (3,192,192 B per the modding skill), DN1 1.42A 2,420,912 B. CPU ColdFire V4e (octabam loads MAIN OS at the same address). Mutable state lives in SDRAM at `0x80000000`; the bootstrap (section 2) is read at load base `0x800003fc`. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} {dn2-skill-firmware} — `digitone-2-internals#a9501e7a` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L73) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Image identity

- [doc] Elektron's own streams keep the furthest match within a 1 MiB window and the longest match at 2,048 bytes; a packer that exceeds them is refused by the build tool. - [doc] Capstone has no ColdFire mode: 98.95 % of boundaries right over `0x40001000` + 64 KB with 201 divergences (it assigns two bytes to each failed instruction and desyncs; it decodes `00 00 2f 0a` as `ori.b`, which ColdFire removed). Stock Ghidra `68000:BE:32:Coldfire` reached 99.76 % over 512 KB but lacks `movclr.l ACCy,Rx` (flow stops at words `a1c0 a3c1 a5c2 a7c3`, so decompilations of the frame ISR and modulation module may be truncated) and gets MSAC-with-load wrong (accumulator selection inverted). digikit's `68000:BE:32:ColdfireEMAC` module fixes this - re-import rather than switching language on an existing program. Auto-analysis of the 3.19 MB 1.11 MAIN OS takes about 128 s; close the Ghidra GUI before headless runs; some large switches report "Could not recover jumptable" and must be read as assembly. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} — `digitone-2-internals#62897b44` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:133](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L133) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)

- [doc] Front-panel LEDs: the LED driver `0x40132148(id, value)` remembers the last value per LED and sends only changes; `LedManager` (pointer `0x446478e0`) is the only route to it, and on each refresh (`0x4002c854`) the first write to an LED wins. Trig keys are logical LED ids 26-41. The palette is uploaded in three sets (one per LED INTENSITY): index 0 off, 1 backlight white, then eight hues of 16 levels each (red 2-17, green 18-33, blue 34-49, yellow 50-65, cyan 66-81, magenta 82-97, white 98-113, orange 114-129), 130-135 special. - [doc] Porting: 1.11 and 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes; about 48.7 % of 48-byte windows from 1.11 appear verbatim in 1.12 but at 535 different offset shifts - fixed-address patches do not port; locate hook points by masked byte patterns (`find`/`expect` fields) and pin every mod to its build by hash. - [doc] Rules for a new OS version (dnfw): compare decoded content (`dnfw diff`), never compressed bytes; use `--strings` as a filter only; read the densest change blocks first (a relink gives many small blocks, a rewrite one large one); check bootstrap and updater separately (the updater matters for recovery); re-locate every patch via `find`/`expect` and name the target build; examine unfamiliar sections (id 8) before relying on the image; mangled storage-struct names show which persisted state changed. The compression and signing scheme was unchanged in 1.11 and the codec limits were measured on 1.11. `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions} — `digitone-2-internals#e912d503` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:194](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L194) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
- [doc] Section 2 is 30,302 bytes; header `[u32 payload_size = 0x7656][u32 0x80010000]` (the second word is not the load base); load base `0x800003fc` incl. the 8-byte header, payload runs at `0x80000404`; status strings READY TO RECEIVE `0x80006603`, RECEIVING... `0x80006614`, UPGRADING... `0x800065e6`, "BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE" at payload offset `0x602c`. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap} — `digitone-2-internals#6816ef39` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:197](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L197) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
- [doc] Receive phase: start marker `0x7F` (kind 1) records the total packet count and starting sequence number; data packets `0x7E` are sequence-checked, their checksum verified over 119 bytes and 101 decoded bytes copied to the buffer; end marker (kind 2) verifies totals. The progress bar measures reception only (`received * 128 / total`). A bad sequence number or checksum sets the state to 0 and the transfer silently stops - no retransmit. Transport is one-way DIN MIDI at 31,250 baud. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap} — `digitone-2-internals#382981ac` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:198](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L198) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
- [doc] Write phase: the receive buffer is RAM at `0x40000000` holding `[u32 size][u32 checksum][container]`; the container check sums `(word_index ^ word)` over `size/4` words from `0x40000008`; flash is erased in 256 KB blocks from `0x80000` and the raw container is written in 512-byte chunks. No decompression happens here - the updater and MAIN OS decompress sections on the next boot (which is why the in-place loader margin matters). The page does not mention any seal/signature verification in this path. A different routine (`FUN_80011844`) flashes a single small section with a CRC (residue `0xDEBB20E3`) and 64 KB caps - not the recovery path. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap} — `digitone-2-internals#4cbfe562` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:199](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L199) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
- [doc] The arp is part of the voice interrupt; its only output is the internal voice allocator `FUN_4002a6a2`, nothing on that path creates a MIDI event. Barriers: UI gating by `FUN_40031274` (isMidiTrack) at the ARP key `0x4005f9b6`, menu auto-close `0x400187ea`, LED `0x40060dde`; the step handler `FUN_400d99de` sends MIDI tracks to `FUN_400d8cbe`; live keys on a MIDI track go straight to the MIDI task via `FUN_4012bb90`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp} — `digitone-2-internals#6df979b7` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:216](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L216) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
- [doc] Data: arp settings per track sound record at `kit+0x34+t*0x48b` (`+0x15f` mode, `+0x160` speed, `+0x161` range, `+0x162` note length, `+0x164` step mask, `+0x166..0x175` offsets); track MIDI mask s16 at `kit+0x5cda`; events are 0x6c bytes (alloc `FUN_40138cb6`, schedule `FUN_40138e3c`), MIDI events 0x60 bytes, MIDI task queue `0x445ff870`, free list head `0x4460f4b8` (2,048 entries), MIDI output byte count `0x44600ca0` (8-bit). The arp self-tick is a type-9 event every 90,000 units (1/60 step); one interrupt pass is ~0.67 ms. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp} — `digitone-2-internals#83d81c4e` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:217](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L217) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
- [doc] Hazards for any MIDI-generating mod: the event allocator `FUN_4012a6e8` does not check for an empty free list (test `0x4460f4b8` first); MIDI events take the untransposed note (the task transposes); source byte `[0xd]` 1 = sequencer (subject to mute/solo), 2 = live; length `0x7f` (INF) hangs notes in the MIDI task; the 8-bit output count wraps above 255 bytes per message; latency ~one pass plus DIN serialisation (~0.96 ms per 3-byte note); vector 191 (voice interrupt) is not modelled by the emulator by default. Design options range from UI-only (~0 bytes) to sequenced trigs with p-locks (~850 bytes). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp} — `digitone-2-internals#62484eb7` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md:218](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-internals.md#L218) · Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
- [doc] `load = exec * 2 + 0x28000000`. Code addresses count 16-bit parcels (VISA), and the entry `0x001c12e2` lands exactly on a loaded region; all 591 of 591 `0x1c`-space jump targets fit. - [doc] Samples travel over USB as SysEx (`dn2samples.py`: hello, send, save, load, forget, lib-send/list/delete/info; Elektron Transfer must be closed). They are written first to a mirror in ColdFire RAM, then fed to the DSP over a TDM "fast link" at about 0.7 MB/s (about 124 words per packet, 1,500 packets/s). Frames are sent first and the directory last so no slot points at missing audio; each 64 KB chunk loaded into the DSP is checked with a VERIFY sum and resent on failure. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#2f138fc8` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L34) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
- [doc] +Drive regions: pool image from sector `0x600000` (3 GiB) with a header sector (`DN2P` in v0.15, `DN2Q` in v0.16) holding length and checksum - the stock storage code does not use anything above 2,224 MiB; library from sector `0x700000` to the end of the device (~20 GB) with a superblock (`DN2L`), an index of 2,048 64-byte entries and up to 64 folders; each library sample is checked with adler-32 before its index entry is written. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#1ea96d8a` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L35) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
- [doc] DSP RAM pool: base at DSP address `0x84000000` in the 512 MB DDR; directory magic `SMP1` (count + 128 entries of address, frames, rate, spare) then the frames. A power-on RAM check (`CMD_PROBE`) fills and reads back 256 KB blocks at 143 MB and 256 MB+; if it fails or gets no answer within 4 s the pool stays at 128 MB. Pool sizes by version: 5 MB (v0.14-v0.15), 128 MB (v0.16: 96 MB samples + 32 MB recordings), 400 MB (v0.22+: 0..96 MB and 128..400 MB samples, 32 MB between for recordings, no more than ~5.5 min of recordings). Up to 122 user slots (SAMP 1..122), 124..127 for the recorder. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#feaa9566` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L38) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
- [doc] Formats: inputs 8/16/24/32-bit PCM or 32-bit float at any rate, mono or stereo; stored as int16 frames in the pool (the doc is inconsistent - an older section says float32); each sample plays at its own rate; recordings 48 kHz int16, peaks between 64 and 32,700 are normalised to 32,700. Slices (max 64): from cue points, `grid:N`, onsets or none; stored with the sample (format word bits 8..15 = count) or, for slices made on the instrument, in a 768-byte area in the last 128 KB of the recordings area (bit 16 marks it). `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#7114f90a` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L39) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)

Boot ladder snapshots at 60M/120M/200M/280M/400M instructions; on 1.11 only the 400M rung draws frames. DMA timer 3 at 30 Hz and PIT2 are required or the main task blocks forever. Panel: 55 buttons and 10 encoders; code = channel*8 + bit + 1 for buttons, channel + 1 for encoders; channel 6 is non-linear (code 0x00 is shared by (6,2) and (6,3)); the wire carries a whole-channel state mask and the firmware XORs it against the last state to detect edges; 1024-byte framebuffers flushed by `panel_diff`. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator} — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#216f3666` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L45) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)

- [doc] Which traps are armed: startup enables only ILOPI (illegal opcode, bit 4) and PARI (L1 parity, bit 3) besides the RTOS timer and software interrupts. FP-exception interrupts (FIXI, FLTOI, FLTUI, FLTII) are not enabled: a NaN in TRUNC/FIX sets only a sticky flag. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#5e78ae90` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:64](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L64) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
- [doc] EMUI, PARI and ILOPI record an error code and return address (DN2 1.11 at DM `0x26ef88-0x26ef94`: `0x507` EMUI, `0x502` PARI, `0x501` ILOPI), then jump to `idle; jump .` inside the handler, forever. `[doc]` — `digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc#086d889b` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md:65](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md#L65) · Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
- [doc] Encoding census: for every instruction you add, its shape (registers and constants blanked) is looked up in stock real code; bits that are constant in every stock instance must match - catches encodings a decoder accepts but stock never emits (the negative-shift sign-bit case). Shape census: lists instruction shapes stock never uses - not an error, but each must be justified from the PRM. The skill's assembler decodes every emitted instruction and compares it with the intended text, and its 48-bit packer schedules loop bodies so they stay hwrules-safe. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts} — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#430eda3b` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:58](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L58) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
- [doc] Framing: `F0 00 20 3C 10 00 <8-in-7 encoded body> F7`; body = sequence (2 bytes, big-endian), `00 00`, opcode, payload; the reply opcode = request OR 0x80. Opcodes seen: `0x01` ping (device name and opcode list), `0x04` screenshot, `0x50` OsUpgradeStart (u32 size big-endian, "sysex", auto-commit byte), `0x51` OsUpgradeWrite (2 KB blocks with CRC32), `0x52` OsUpgradeEnd (1 commit / 0 cancel). OS 1.11's RPC handlers read every u32 big-endian. Upstream documentation: dnfw `docs/midi-rpc.md` (derived from Elektroid). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts} — `digitone-2-os111-firmware-map#6169a1fe` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-firmware-map.md#L61) · Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)

More RAM above is plausible but must be verified (fill, reboot, read). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#5171ef65` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L30) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
- [doc] Side channels: the DMA moves 1374 halfwords; the 30 halfwords after the 2688-byte frame (data halves of TX entries 1344..1373) are never rewritten by the stock driver and reach the DSP - write packets there from a hook just before the driver call (header word + checksum, round-robin if larger). Return: reply word 0 = the DSP's cycle count for the block (a load meter), +0x16 = master compressor gain reduction, `+0xa9c..+0xabc` (ColdFire `0x80005e40`, 16 u16) is unused by stock and free as a DSP -> ColdFire channel. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#6862a7ac` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:50](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L50) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
- [doc] Voices are not tracks. The DSP renders 16 voices; the ColdFire allocates them per note and copies the track's sound into the voice record; unison uses several voices per note. Note path, lock applier, LFO evaluator and per-voice mirror blocks all work per voice - map voice -> track everywhere. The skill calls this the #1 bug source. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#1be77337` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L52) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
- [doc] Hooks are `jsr stub` / `jmp stub` over N displaced bytes; the build asserts the displaced bytes match stock. Arguments on the stack, result in d0 (GCC ColdFire convention); d0, d1, a0, a1 are scratch. A hook in the middle of a function must preserve d0, d1, a0, a1 for the code after it; a hook replacing a function's entry must preserve the callee's exit d0, d1, a0, a1 and copy every stack argument. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#2734bfcf` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L55) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [doc] `movem` accepts only `(An)` or `d16(An)`: push with `lea -12(%sp),%sp; movem.l %d1/%a0-%a1,(%sp)`; recount `sp@(n)` after every push. Every symbol a hook references must be an entry or `--gc-sections` drops it. No libc: zero-initialised locals become `memset` calls and the link fails - use static const data or field-by-field stores. Appended asm after `.bss` lands in zeroed memory and the boot dies in the exception reporter. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#472b0b66` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L56) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [doc] Compiler: m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os`; build system `dnfw.patch.cbuild` with `cfmod.Mod` as startup loader. cfmod's loader cave: 138 bytes at `0x4028da6e` (copies the appended area to its load address at boot and calls your init); proven asm cave: 170 bytes at `0x4028ea02`; never use the ~64 KB of zeros near `0x402e2000` (the `.data` initializer). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#4f43aa19` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:57](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L57) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [doc] Slot bounds: every stock value, lock and LFO routine bounds `slot <= 100`; slots 0, 65 and 100 are holes; a sound stores 101 u16 values at `sound + 0x14 + 2*slot`. A new slot means hooking every one of those routines. Your own p-lock record headers need an ID no stock slot uses, and copy/paste/recount/clear routines must skip them. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#94923311` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:59](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L59) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [doc] Pitfalls: a new parameter record needs a guard record after the last entry (the drawer reads one past); enum formatters print ERR past their table; every per-sound side table needs a reset hook (sound reset and kit creation reuse memory); sound save rewrites LFO DEST words in slots 4, 12 and 20; skipping the stock redraw request can add ~1 s UI latency on hardware (the emulator does not show it); never draw the stock screen and then patch it (panel can receive a frame mid-draw); a new machine type means re-entering every per-type accessor bounded by `type <= 4`. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#0f4394c2` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:60](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L60) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
- [doc] SHARC (`sim.py`/`simc.py`, ~200 blocks/s with the C core, ~7 on PyPy, ~1 on CPython): logic and arithmetic in the real frame, stock-vs-mod A/B, memory footprint, the PRM rules it encodes. Cannot cover timing, caches, stalls, interrupts, DMA, branch predictor, ECC, boot-ROM loading, power-on memory contents; "instruction counts under-predict the unit's load". One-time boot ~4 min (`dn2setup.py --boot`). `[doc]` — `digitone-2-os111-reference#b0d02d46` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:74](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L74) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
- [doc] ColdFire (digikit + `fastemu.py` + `cfkit.py`, 10-30 M instr/s): main OS in Unicorn with HLEs for flash, SD, panel, screen; boots to the main screen (~1 min first time, cached). Divergences: idle skip fires widget timers far more often (redraws look smoother than the unit's ~1/s); encoders register in bursts (single detents do nothing, use `turn_to` with 11-detent messages); holds need >= 12 M instructions; keys right after encoder bursts may drop; Python hooks do not fire under the fast stepper; panel TX ring is never drained; no DTCN2 timer; plain Unicorn halves fractional EMAC results (use digiemu's patched Unicorn); test from several start offsets - a real bug fails at every offset. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#de90eaff` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:75](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L75) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
- [doc] Measuring on hardware: a screenshot RPC (`dn2rpc.c shot`) lets a mod publish a debug page; DSP load = reply word 0; ColdFire ISR time = DTCN2 stamps at hook entry and before the RTE (`0x40027bbe`). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#739f5c42` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:76](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L76) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
- [doc] Flash with `scripts/rpc_flash.py IMAGE.syx` over USB or Elektron Transfer and confirm on the unit. Keep USB quiet for ~90 s during the flash write. The first upload after boot is lost with auto-commit; kill stale flasher processes before rerunning. Python + mido can hang at exit on CoreMIDI. Avoid flashing or measuring during heavy local jobs (USB MIDI timing). Raw SysEx over USB to the running OS is ignored (only the update protocol works). Recovery: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~12-15 min. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-setup} — `digitone-2-os111-reference#9517cadb` [hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md:79](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md#L79) · Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Flashing notes from the skill's setup
- [doc] Toolchain: `gcc-m68k-linux-gnu` / `binutils-m68k-linux-gnu` with `-mcpu=5475` on Linux/WSL; on macOS build GCC 13 and binutils 2.42 from source; PyPy 3.10+, `cffi`, `mido`, `python-rtmidi`; dnfw from angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore; digikit (the skill clones m-dwyer/digikit and applies `scripts/digikit-local.patch`). - [doc] 16 tracks, each audio (SYN machine) or MIDI; 16 audio voices (one per track) each with SYN machine, bit reduction, filter, amp and LFO; 12 V DC via PSU-3c; balanced/unbalanced 1/4" I/O, inputs also over USB; MIDI IN, OUT/SYNC A, THRU/SYNC B (SYNC outputs can send DIN sync); USB type B, class compliant, audio + MIDI, Overbridge. Wait at least 30 s after power-off before powering on again; ambient max 40 deg C. `[doc]` {dn2-manual} — `digitone-2#cba013a4` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L18) · Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
- [doc] Data model: +Drive holds up to 128 projects and a library of 2,048 presets; a project = 128 patterns (8 banks x 16), 16 songs, a 128-preset pool and general settings; a pattern holds up to 16 presets (one per track), sequencer data, TRIG page settings, BPM, length, swing, time signature, MIDI track parameters; a preset holds SYN1, SYN2, FLTR, AMP and LFO pages. Digitone I projects can be imported but patterns may differ - re-save on Digitone II before exporting. `[doc]` {dn2-manual} — `digitone-2#c67bcb0a` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L19) · Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
- [doc] MIDI in: notes 0-15 trigger tracks 1-16 (default channels), notes 16-84 (E2-C7) play the active track chromatically (C5 = 60 is middle C), program change 0-127 selects patterns A01-H16, tap tempo by note C0 on the FX CONTROL channel; MIDI tracks: up to 16 notes per step, pitch bend, aftertouch, 16 assignable CCs (CC1-8 on the FLTR page, 9-16 on AMP); the lowest-numbered track wins when tracks share a channel. TRIG modes: TRACKS, VELOCITIES (TRIG 1-15 = velocity 8..120 in steps of 8, TRIG 16 = 127), RETRIGS (1/1 ... 1/64). `[doc]` {dn2-manual} — `digitone-2#1fa74ef2` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L20) · Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)

- [doc] Each parameter is one 60-byte row. Table base `0x401f83a4`, stock 321 rows. Offsets: `+0x00` group (set/page family), `+0x04` k (the slot that holds the value in its set), `+0x08..0x14` min/max/default/bipolar, `+0x18` MIDI CC, `+0x1c` NRPN, `+0x20` Overbridge id, `+0x28..0x38` names/formatter/suffix. A separate RAM display table holds glyph, lock flags and randomiser data. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#48e5ba3e` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:78](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L78) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] Row ids are not saved; projects store values by slot k through fixed k-to-stored-id tables. Slot maps and CC/NRPN maps are rebuilt from the table at each boot (`0x400dc634`); page records are built at boot from code constants (`0x400c2c4e`). Moving the table does not change project storage; new rows do, via their k and display flags. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#761fcfc8` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:79](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L79) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] Grown table at `0x47D00000`, room for 384 rows (`0x180`), copied at boot by `pg_boot` (called from `0x40000568`). New row ids `0x141`-`0x17f` (63 ids); the same-length-edit ceiling is `0x1e0` (480 rows). 56 address operands in 53 functions had to be redirected; 57 row-count compares changed (`#0x141`->`#0x180`, `#0x140`->`#0x17f`; five look similar and stay). The display-table reader at `0x400c257c` has its first 10 bytes turned into a jump plus two nops. The MIDI input cache (33 constants in five functions) grows by 12,852 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#fc89114e` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:80](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L80) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] Map builders hold 101 entries each, so k must stay in range (0..100 for sound/FX/MIDI, 0..25 for trig). Stock saves FX k 25-69 only; FX k 70+ and sound k 65 and 100 are not saved. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#e77da10d` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L83) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] Rules for a new row: use a free k in the set's table, one row per k (the last row written wins and can silently replace a stock knob); value 0 must keep classic behaviour (existing projects store 0 in slots stock has no row for); send-FX rows set `flags_set = 8` so they are never lockable; synth rows use free saved k values (FM Tone 34, 49; WaveTone 50-64; FM Drum 55-64; Swarmer 33-64); no randomiser; MIDI: no CC already in the set's map, none in 32-63, none taken by the CC parser (1, 2, 6, 64, 66, 94, 98, 99, 110, 120, 121, 123), NRPN 398 at most; Overbridge id outside stock's 0..387 (e.g. `0x400`+n, untested with the plugin). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#69bb819c` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:84](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L84) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] P-lock trap: a row is lockable when display flag bits 0 and 3 are clear; locks are stored as (track, k), so an FX row with k 70 could create a lock on a sound's slot 70, which stock would play back. A bad row can write past map tables, replace a stock knob, or leave stray p-locks that persist after returning to stock. A project saved on a grown build and loaded on stock 1.12 is untested on hardware. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#efe82ef0` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:85](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L85) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
- [doc] Checks used: brick checker 12/12 for GT00/GT01 ("a pass is not proof for code changes"), `scripts/t65_build.py check_rows` for FX rows, `pg_boot` only skips ids outside `0x141`-`0x17f` (it does not check k, flags, CCs or Overbridge ids), an emulator run of 7,100 MIDI messages giving the same 991 parameter sets as baseline. Never flash `param-test-dn2` or `fx-page2-dn2`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table} — `digitone-2#43ddb6ee` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:86](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L86) · Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)

- [doc] A stock DN2 has no sample filesystem, and a mod that mounts one must also create it (armio R012, 2026-11-03). R012 mounted an existing sample filesystem but did not create one on a unit that never had it; on such a unit Transfer showed 0% Free / 0 bytes, uploads stalled and connections failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects. The bug was found by new users; the author's own unit had storage prepared during development, which is why owner testing missed it. A test on a freshly flashed stock unit is the only check that catches this. `[doc]` {armio-samples} ([I12](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i12-a-sample-machine-mod-could-not-create-the-storage-it-needed)) — `digitone-2#f87231c1` [hardware/devices/digitone-2.md:98](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2.md#L98) · Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)

- [untagged] The whole container is staged in RAM; flash is untouched until the last message. A transfer cut before the footer leaves the screen on "Receiving" and nothing validated, erased or written.
